post.caption: Mozart wanted pockets for five watches. In 1777, Mannheim's court gave Mozart a golden watch. He wrote that he would rather have cash for the road. Then he added that he now had five watches. His plan was a little watch pocket in each pair of trousers. He would wear two watches to see a great lord. The real reason was to stop people giving him more watches. In 1778, he wrote that one watch had gone to practice. Editors read that as pawned, for five louis d'or at most. He swapped two watches for a Paris watch worth twenty louis d'or.
